widget.prompt: What kind of number is an even number plus an even number?

options.label: even
options.feedback: Correct — an even number plus an even number pairs every leftover, so the sum always lands even.

options.label: odd
options.feedback: Try 3 + 5 or 4 + 6: the leftovers pair with each other, leaving none — that is even, not odd.

options.label: sometimes even, sometimes odd
options.feedback: Parity here never wavers — the leftover structure forces the same result every single time.

options.label: impossible to know
options.feedback: You can know without computing: track the leftovers and the parity is decided.

steps.body: One more, for the road — but this time, check the PARTS, not just the sum.
explanationVariants: 9 + 9 joins two EQUAL groups; 8 + 6 does not.
Landing on an even number is not enough — the parts must match.

widget.prompt: Maggie lines up 9 + 9 and 8 + 6. Both add up to an even number. Which one is a DOUBLE?

options.label: 9 + 9, because both parts are the same number
options.feedback: Correct — 9 + 9 joins two EQUAL groups of 9. Equal parts are what make a double.

options.label: 8 + 6, because it also lands on an even number
options.feedback: 8 + 6 = 14 is even, but 8 and 6 are not equal — landing on an even number does not make an addition a double.

options.label: Both, because every even sum comes from a double
options.feedback: Not every even sum is a double — 8 + 6 is even, but its two parts are not equal.

options.label: Neither, because 9 + 9 is odd
options.feedback: 9 + 9 = 18, which is even, not odd — doubles always land on an even number.
